clue.text: Worthless article by writer on the stimulant effect of alcohol

indicators.note: in an across clue, the writer placed on the end of the first piece follows it

parts.note: a drink's kick is the jolt it gives
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Someone credits a playwright's essay with explaining why a drink perks you up.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle or bauble of no value is the old meaning of this word, from French quelque chose.

clue.text: Confess to being over the hill as a stand-off

parts.note: a speaker owning up says 'I am', contracted to I'M
passé means past its best, no longer young

explanation.surface: An ageing negotiator admits they are past it, ending the talks in deadlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock where neither side can advance is the same as a standoff.

clue.text: Animal tipped to win by the book .

parts.note: a kid is a young goat
in racing a tipster's nap is their most confident selection, so a napped horse is tipped to win

explanation.surface: A goat is a racing tipster's banker selection, judging by the form guide.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on to the next one; 'by' is a link word. The book is Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's novel of David Balfour's abduction is a famous title, so it serves as a specific example of a book.

clue.text: … Basil's simple book

parts.note: basil is a herb, a 'simple' is an old word for a medicinal plant, and a volume describing such plants is the reading

explanation.surface: A man named Basil has written an easy-to-read volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil looks like a man's name, but it is the plant; 'simple' looks like 'easy' but is the noun for a healing herb.
explanation.definitionFit: An old book describing plants and their medicinal uses, like those of Gerard or Culpeper, is called this.

clue.text: Islander's so-called tenor was to run the Empire

indicators.note: the islander's description is only what it is called, a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a man of the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast, is a Wight man
a burden is the main theme or gist, as is the tenor of a speech

explanation.surface: An island man's supposed gist was that the Empire should be governed.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is Kipling's, for the supposed duty of colonisers to govern others; 'was' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's poem cast imperial rule as an obligation the colonisers carried, the job of governing an empire.

clue.text: One should have a good nap in this coat

definitions.text: One should have a good nap in this coat

parts.words: One should have a good nap in this coat
parts.note: reads as a coat to sleep in, but nap is the raised pile on a heavy woollen cloth

explanation.surface: A coat that is perfect for snoozing in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nap' suggests a doze; here it is the fuzzy surface of the thick woollen fabric the coat is made from, with toggle fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded toggle-fastened coat of heavy woollen cloth is named after the Belgian town of Duffel.

clue.text: Girl might be said to be explosive

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, and spoken quickly it becomes another word

parts.note: Dinah, a girl's name, followed by the word might

explanation.surface: A girl is reported to have a fiery temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying 'Dinah might' runs the two words together into the name of an explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobel's blasting substance of nitroglycerine is an explosive.

clue.text: Give prominence to exploit on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue the deed sits on top of the river

parts.note: an exploit is a heroic deed or feat
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A daring stunt on the water earns headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight something or make it a centrepiece is to give it prominence.

clue.text: No note about Greensleeves playing in the refreshment interval

indicators.note: the remaining letters are played around with into a new order
with no note and no about means these pieces are dropped from the tune's name

parts.note: G is a note of the musical scale
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A performance of Greensleeves with no notes about it goes on during the tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' takes G and RE from the front of GREENSLEEVES, leaving ENSLEEVES; 'playing' rearranges those letters. 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mid-morning break for tea and a biscuit is a British custom of refreshment.

clue.text: Webster seen, say, with cockney girl

indicators.note: the word is to be taken as spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: spied means seen or caught sight of
a cockney drops the H of her, giving 'er

explanation.surface: A girl from London's East End was seen with a dictionary-maker called Webster.
explanation.walkthrough: Webster looks like the dictionary-maker but is a weaver of webs. Cockney is the working-class East London dialect, which drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: The creature that spins webs is literally a web-maker.

clue.text: Introduce fashionable new star to "The Outsiders"

parts.note: in means trendy or fashionable
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens, once thought new

indicators.note: the outside letters of the word The are taken

explanation.surface: A trendy rising talent is cast in a production of The Outsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring in something new, as a method or idea, is to introduce it.

clue.text: Get off without publicity in a scrape

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to get off is to escape
an ad is an advertisement, publicity

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble wriggles free while avoiding the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here. 'In a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless adventure or mischievous exploit lands one in a scrape.

clue.text: Full-blown bloom

definitions.meaning: to come to full flower, to ripen

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe reaching full development, as an adjective of ripeness and as a verb of flowering.

clue.text: Beat time

definitions.meaning: the pulse or pace of music
musical time, the speed at which a piece is played

explanation.definitionFit: The speed of a piece of music is both its beat and its time in musical language.

clue.text: Firm line taken by lofty pedestrian

parts.note: tight means firm or taut
a rope is a line

explanation.surface: A firm policy is adopted by a haughty walker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lofty' suggests snooty; the pedestrian is literally high up, a circus funambulist.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-wire walker crosses a taut cable above the crowd, the route an aerial walker takes.

clue.text: Pair click when brought together in dance

definitions.text: Pair click when brought together in dance

parts.words: Pair click when brought together in dance
parts.note: a couple getting on well when matched up on the dance floor, or two shells struck together to click in Spanish dance

explanation.surface: Two partners hit it off when they meet at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Click' suggests rapport; here it is a literal clicking sound made by hand-held shells in flamenco.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish percussion of two shells struck together in the hand makes a clicking accompaniment.

clue.text: Verdict setting a difficult problem, say, for the Archdeacon

indicators.note: the word is taken as spoken, keeping only its sound

parts.note: a knot is a tricky problem to untangle
pro means in favour of
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: A court finding that sets a knotty puzzle for a senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a verdict available only in Scottish law, between guilty and not guilty. 'Setting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish court may return this outcome when guilt is suspected but evidence is insufficient.

clue.text: Staying at school and getting on

definitions.meaning: living in at a residential school
climbing aboard a train, ship or plane

explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who lives in at school is a boarder, and passengers entering a vessel or aircraft board it.

clue.text: Talk about the old firm trading originally in Africa

indicators.note: the chatter is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: gas is idle chatter
taken as written
Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: the first letter of trading is taken

explanation.surface: Gossip concerns a long-established company that first traded in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: this was the colonial name for what is now Ghana, in West Africa. 'The' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The British colony that became Ghana was a region of West Africa.

clue.text: Tenniel's letters could be forgiving

indicators.note: the letters of the illustrator's name could be rearranged into another word

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Sir John Tenniel, illustrator of Alice, writes notes that might be indulgent.
explanation.walkthrough: John Tenniel was the Victorian cartoonist who illustrated Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being merciful or indulgent toward faults is a forgiving disposition.

clue.text: Wounds from shots

definitions.meaning: attempts, as in having a go

explanation.definitionFit: A knife thrust wounds someone, and a stab at something is an attempt or try.

clue.text: Sausages displayed in crates

definitions.meaning: British slang for sausages, which can burst with a bang when fried
old rattletrap cars, called crates or ... in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Displayed in' are link words; 'crates' suggests boxes but means decrepit old cars.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the same word for a sausage and for a noisy old jalopy.

clue.text: Painting in a health resort in ancient Greece

indicators.note: the art is placed within the resort

parts.note: a spa is a resort with healing waters
art such as painting

explanation.surface: A painting is on show at a wellness retreat in classical Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer was a city-state in ancient Greece. 'A' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The warrior city-state of the Peloponnese was a power in classical Greece.

clue.text: Supply vessel requiring careful handling

definitions.meaning: a boat ferrying supplies to a larger ship
sore or sensitive, needing gentle treatment

explanation.definitionFit: A small boat serving a larger ship has this name, and a sensitive spot or delicate issue is also described by it.

clue.text: Ring up — I'm involved in adjudicating

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up together into a new order

explanation.surface: A caller phones and says they are taking part in judging.
explanation.definitionFit: Refereeing or judging a contest is adjudicating it.

clue.text: American passerine ready for cooking

parts.note: reads as a songbird prepared for roasting, a bird fit for the kitchen range

explanation.surface: A small American songbird has been prepared for roasting.
explanation.walkthrough: The American warbler is named for its domed, oven-shaped nest; the clue jokes that it is ready for the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American warbler builds a domed nest like a baker's kiln, hence its name.

clue.text: A sound theatrical entertainment in retrospect

indicators.note: the word is taken as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: a revue is a stage show of sketches and songs

explanation.surface: A good stage show looks back at the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sound' reads as 'a good', but 'sound' is the homophone signal; 'A' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey looking back over past events is a retrospect.

clue.text: Putting away etching

definitions.meaning: corroding, as acid eats into metal

explanation.definitionFit: Putting away a meal is consuming it, and acid etching a plate is corroding or eating into it.

clue.text: To come to the point, it's parsimony

parts.note: to near is to approach or come to
a ness is a headland or point, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Getting to the point, someone admits to being stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is an old word for mean with money. 'It's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinginess is the quality of being close-fisted, which old British usage called near.
